network.tdh.verify.metadataDescription: Every day, Rust, Python and 6529.io TDH side by side, with every difference explained.
network.tdh.verify.title: TDH verification
network.tdh.verify.lede: Every day, the TDH of every collector is computed three ways and compared: by the validators’ Rust core, by the Python reference, and by 6529.io’s current backend. This page shows the results, every difference and its cause. Holders appear only as labels.
network.tdh.verify.sample.title: Sample: the daily job’s own files for 14 and 15 October 2026.
network.tdh.verify.sample.body: These are real runs of the Rust core and the Python reference, made before the Rust core netted within a transaction (D131). That is why two holders differ from 6529.io each day; with netting, every identity and wallet is equal on both days. Published daily reports replace this sample once they are connected.
network.tdh.verify.awaiting.title: Daily reports start on 16 October 2026.
network.tdh.verify.awaiting.body: The first one appears here after its run. Until then, the evidence behind TDH-v1 is on the specification page.

network.tdh.verify.diff.heading: Differences
network.tdh.verify.diff.lede: A difference is any record that is not equal in every compared field. An identity and its wallets are one case, with a class and, when known, a cause. Holders appear only as labels: this page names no one, but each value is also in 6529.io’s public upload of that day, next to its address.
network.tdh.verify.diff.emptyFiltered: No differences in this class on this day.
network.tdh.verify.diff.caption: Differences on cycle {cycle}: {shown} of {total} holders shown
network.tdh.verify.class.A.body: Explained by a deliberate difference between TDH-v1 and the old backend (a DEV item).
network.tdh.verify.class.B.body: Explained by a known issue in the old backend (a BUG item).
network.tdh.verify.class.C.body: A defect in the new software, for example Rust and Python disagree.
network.tdh.verify.class.D.body: Not yet explained. Every difference starts here until it is classified, and raises an alarm.
network.tdh.verify.class.note: Class A and B differences are explained, not accepted: the owner still decides what to do with each.
network.tdh.verify.cause.DEV-2: DEV-2 is the order of movements. Across transactions TDH-v1 keeps on-chain order, even within one block, where 6529.io’s backend uses its own order; within one transaction it nets each wallet’s movements (D131). These runs did not yet net, so a token sent out and back in one transaction restarted its age, while 6529.io kept it. The Rust core now nets, and such cases agree. The difference that can remain is a sale and a purchase of one card in different transactions of one block; it ends at the cutover.

network.tdh.verify.method.heading: How this works
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.title: The same snapshot.
network.tdh.verify.method.snapshot.body: All three use the snapshot block of the day, the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.title: Independent computation.
network.tdh.verify.method.inputs.body: The Rust core reads the day’s events from Ethereum and computes TDH-v1. The Python reference computes from the same input, after checking its SHA-256, so the two compare computation, not reading Ethereum. 6529.io’s values come from the files it publishes every day on Arweave, accepted only when the upload key’s signature and the file’s size and data root verify. 6529.io’s values are the object under test, never an input.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.title: Exact comparison.
network.tdh.verify.method.exact.body: The TDH fields of every identity and wallet are compared for exact equality, with no tolerance: boost, boosted TDH, TDH and whole days, per collection and per token, plus record counts, totals and the snapshot block. The upload’s other columns, ranks, balance and set counts (BUG-15) and display names, are listed but not compared.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.title: Classification.
network.tdh.verify.method.classes.body: Each difference is classed A to D, and only known differences are explained: any other raises an alarm.
network.tdh.verify.method.after.title: After the cutover,
network.tdh.verify.method.after.body: 6529.io runs the Rust core, so their agreement shows that what is published is what was computed. The Python reference stays the independent check of the computation.
network.tdh.verify.method.validators: Validators will run the same comparison on their own, after they have signed, so 6529.io’s values can never influence their vote.
network.tdh.verify.flow.title: The daily comparison
network.tdh.verify.flow.desc: Two flows meet in the comparison. Ethereum feeds the Rust core, and the Python reference computes from the Rust run’s input. Separately, 6529.io’s backend publishes its upload on Arweave. The comparison publishes the files this page reads.
network.tdh.verify.flow.sameCode: After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the same Rust core.
network.tdh.verify.flow.text: Ethereum → Rust core → Python reference on the same input → Compare. 6529.io backend → Arweave upload → Compare. Compare → published JSON → this page. After the cutover, the 6529.io backend runs the Rust core.

network.tdh.verify.check.heading: Check it yourself
network.tdh.verify.check.intro: What anyone can check today, and what needs the source once it is published.
network.tdh.verify.check.upload: Open 6529.io’s upload for the day on Arweave and add up its boosted TDH column: you get the 6529.io total on this page.
network.tdh.verify.check.block: Open the snapshot block on a block explorer: it is the last block before 00:00 UTC of the day.
network.tdh.verify.check.file: Download the day’s file: every number on this page comes from it.
network.tdh.verify.check.sourceBody: The same day’s run is two commands. The Rust run reads Ethereum and writes its canonical input; the Python reference computes from that input:
